title: Cartesian groupoid pushforward and the restricted ordinary adjunction
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $\mathcal R=(U,R,s,t,c,e,i)$ and $\mathcal R'=(U',R',s',t',c',e',i')$ be groupoids in schemes over $S$ [def-a1-scheme-groupoid-laws]. For either groupoid, a quasi-coherent equivariant module is a quasi-coherent module $M$ on its object scheme [pqf-def-coherent] with an isomorphism $\beta:t^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}s^*M$ [def-pc-module-pullback] satisfying $e^*\beta=1$ and $c^*\beta=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\beta\circ\operatorname{pr}_0^*\beta$; morphisms $a:(M,\beta)\to(N,\gamma)$ obey $s^*a\circ\beta=\gamma\circ t^*a$. Denote this category by $\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal R)$, and similarly for $\mathcal R'$. Suppose morphisms $f_0:U\to U'$ and $f_1:R\to R'$ commute with source, target, identity, inversion and composition, so define a morphism of groupoids $f:\mathcal R\to\mathcal R'$. Assume $f_0$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (inverse images of affine opens are quasi-compact, and its diagonal is quasi-compact), $s',t'$ are flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], and the square with horizontal maps $f_1,f_0$ and vertical maps $t,t'$ is Cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then pullback $f^*(M,\beta)=(f_0^*M,f_1^*\beta)$ and direct image $f_*$ define functors
$$f^*:\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal R')\longrightarrow\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal R),\qquad f_*:\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal R)\longrightarrow\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal R').$$
The underlying module and map of $f_*$ are $f_{0,*}N$ and $f_{0,*}a$. Its equivariant isomorphism is the natural composite
$$(t')^*f_{0,*}N\xrightarrow{b_t}f_{1,*}t^*N\xrightarrow{f_{1,*}\gamma}f_{1,*}s^*N\xrightarrow{b_s^{-1}}(s')^*f_{0,*}N,$$
where $b_t,b_s$ are the canonical flat base-change maps for the target and source squares, respectively. Both maps are isomorphisms, and this composite satisfies the identity and cocycle conditions. The ordinary module-sheaf adjunction restricts to natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal R)}(f^*M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal R')}(M,f_*N).$$
Precisely, the underlying ordinary adjunction transpose of an equivariant map is equivariant, and the inverse ordinary transpose of an equivariant map is equivariant. Thus these bijections specify an adjunction $f^*\dashv f_*$.

proof.text: The target square is Cartesian by assumption. Applying inversion on both arrow schemes exchanges target with source and commutes with $f_1$, so the source square is Cartesian too. Equivalently, on every test scheme an arrow of $\mathcal R'$ and a lift of its target have a unique lift in $\mathcal R$; inversion gives the analogous uniqueness for a specified source. Pullback preserves quasi-coherence by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]. Pull back the identity equation for $\beta$ along $f_0$ and its cocycle equation along $f_2:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R'\times_{s',U',t'}R'$. The groupoid-functor equations identify these with the required equations for $f_1^*\beta$. Pulling back the equation for a morphism gives its equivariance. Functoriality of module pullback gives identities and composition. This constructs $f^*$, without a flatness condition on $f_0$.

source.place: Tag 03LJ, lemma-pullback; Tag 09VH, source square obtained by inversion.

proof.text:
Fix the following notation for comparisons, including non-Cartesian squares. If $p:A\to B$, $q:A'\to B'$, $u:A\to A'$, $v:B\to B'$ satisfy $qu=vp$, write $B_{p,q}:q^*v_*\to u_*p^*$ for the mate of $u^*q^*\cong p^*v^*$. This is [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] with the adjunctions for $v$ and $u$ from [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. For a second square $r:B\to C$, $r':B'\to C'$, $w:C\to C'$, the pasting formula is
$$B_{rp,r'q}=B_{p,q}(r^*(-))\circ q^*B_{r,r'}.$$
Here both sides have source $(r'q)^*w_*$ and target $u_*(rp)^*$. Apply [new-integral-residue-mate-pasting] to the three vertical adjunctions: the inverse mate of the composite on the right is the pasted pullback square; this is the outer pullback square. The latter equality is associativity of the canonical tensor pullback identifications of [def-pc-module-pullback] (on local tensors both send $a\otimes b\otimes m$ to $ab\otimes m$). Injectivity of the inverse mate gives the formula. A square with identity horizontal maps ($u,v$ identities, $p=q$) has comparison the identity, and so does a square with identity vertical maps ($p,q$ identities, $u=v$): after the identifications $\mathrm{id}^*\cong\mathrm{id}$ of [def-pc-module-pullback] the comparison is $u_*\varepsilon_u\circ\eta_{u_*}=1$, by the triangle identity of [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. The comparisons are natural in the module, since units, counits and pullback composition are natural. No invertibility assertion is made here.

source.place: Tag 09VH, omitted comparison coherences; ordinary adjunction and composition: sheaves.tex Tags 0096 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules), 0097 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules).

proof.text:
We will also use the comparison's normalized transpose. In the notation of step 2, let $h:v^*M\to N$ and let $\widehat h:M\to v_*N$ be its ordinary transpose. Under $u^*\dashv u_*$, the transpose of
$$q^*M\xrightarrow{q^*\widehat h}q^*v_*N\xrightarrow{B_{p,q}(N)}u_*p^*N$$
is $p^*h$, with the canonical identification $u^*q^*M\cong p^*v^*M$. Indeed [lem-amb-mate-unit-counit] identifies the transpose of $B_{p,q}(N)$ with $p^*\varepsilon_{v,N}$. Naturality then identifies the displayed transpose with $p^*(\varepsilon_{v,N}\circ v^*\widehat h)=p^*h$. This uses the given ordinary adjunction, not an independently chosen Hom bijection.

source.place: Tag 09VH, last two sentences of proof: restriction of the ordinary module adjunction; expanded counit calculation.

proof.text: For $(N,\gamma)$, the module $F=f_{0,*}N$ is quasi-coherent by [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh], since $f_0$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] in degree zero to each of the Cartesian source and target squares: the horizontal direct-image map is $f_0$, the flat base maps are $s',t'$, and $N$ is quasi-coherent. This gives natural isomorphisms $b_s=B_{s,s'}(N)$ and $b_t=B_{t,t'}(N)$. Define $\delta=b_s^{-1}\circ f_{1,*}\gamma\circ b_t$. It is an isomorphism. If $a:N\to N_1$ is equivariant, naturality of $b_s,b_t$ converts $f_{1,*}(s^*a\circ\gamma)=f_{1,*}(\gamma_1\circ t^*a)$ into $(s')^*f_{0,*}a\circ\delta=\delta_1\circ(t')^*f_{0,*}a$. Thus the ordinary direct-image maps are equivariant; they preserve identities and composition. It remains to verify the two equations for $\delta$.

source.place: Tag 09VH, first and second paragraphs; schemes.tex Tag 01LC (lemma-push-forward-quasi-coherent); coherent.tex Tag 02KH (lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology), i=0.

proof.text: Put $P=R\times_{s,U,t}R$, $P'=R'\times_{s',U',t'}R'$ and let $f_2:P\to P'$ be induced by $f_1$ on both factors. Both projection squares $(\operatorname{pr}_j,\operatorname{pr}'_j)$ with vertical maps $f_2,f_1$ are Cartesian. To see this for $j=0$, fix a lift $a$ of the first arrow $a'$ and a second arrow $b'$ with $t'(b')=s'(a')$. The target-square uniqueness of step 1 lifts $b'$ uniquely with target $s(a)$. For $j=1$, fix $b$ and lift $a'$ with source $t(b)$ using source-square uniqueness. These constructions are functorial on test schemes and are inverse to the fiber-product comparisons by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The map $f_1$ is qcqs, being a base change of $f_0$, by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. The maps $\operatorname{pr}'_0,\operatorname{pr}'_1$ are flat: they are respectively base changes of $t',s'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]. Hence [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom], applied to $f_1$ in degree zero, gives isomorphisms $B_{\operatorname{pr}_j,\operatorname{pr}'_j}(L)$ for every quasi-coherent module $L$ on $R$. In particular take $L=s^*N,t^*N$, which are quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent].

source.place: Tag 09VH: details of the sentence about the cocycle condition, using fiber-product universal properties and Tag 02KH.

proof.text:
For the identity, let $D(L)=B_{e,e'}(L):e'^*f_{1,*}L\to f_{0,*}e^*L$. This comparison exists by step 2, even though $e'$ need not be flat. Pasting the $e$ square with the $s$ square, and with the $t$ square, gives
$$D(s^*N)\circ e'^*b_s=1_F=D(t^*N)\circ e'^*b_t.$$
In particular $D(s^*N)$ is invertible, since $e'^*b_s$ is. Pull back $b_s\delta=f_{1,*}\gamma\,b_t$ along $e'$ and postcompose with $D(s^*N)$. Naturality of $D$ gives
$$e'^*\delta=f_{0,*}(e^*\gamma)=1_F.$$
Thus the identity law holds. This cancellation only uses the isomorphisms already obtained in step 4.

source.place: Tag 09VH, omitted identity check for the constructed direct-image equivariance.

proof.text:
On $P$ write $u=t\operatorname{pr}_0=tc$, $v=s\operatorname{pr}_1=sc$, and $w=s\operatorname{pr}_0=t\operatorname{pr}_1$; use primes for the corresponding maps on $P'$. Set $C_u=B_{u,u'}(N)$, and similarly $C_v,C_w$. By pasting (step 2), $C_u=B_{\operatorname{pr}_0,\operatorname{pr}'_0}(t^*N)\circ\operatorname{pr}'_0{}^*b_t$, and $C_v=B_{\operatorname{pr}_1,\operatorname{pr}'_1}(s^*N)\circ\operatorname{pr}'_1{}^*b_s$; both are isomorphisms by steps 4--5. Naturality and pasting give the three equations
$$C_v c'^*\delta=f_{2,*}(c^*\gamma)C_u,$$
$$C_w\operatorname{pr}'_0{}^*\delta=f_{2,*}(\operatorname{pr}_0^*\gamma)C_u,$$
$$C_v\operatorname{pr}'_1{}^*\delta=f_{2,*}(\operatorname{pr}_1^*\gamma)C_w.$$
For the first, apply $B_{c,c'}$ to $c'^*(b_s\delta=f_{1,*}\gamma\,b_t)$, move $\gamma$ across by naturality, and identify the two outer composites by pasting; the other two equations use the respective projection squares in the identical substitution. Multiplying the last two equations and using $c^*\gamma=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\gamma\circ\operatorname{pr}_0^*\gamma$ gives $C_v c'^*\delta=C_v(\operatorname{pr}'_1{}^*\delta\circ\operatorname{pr}'_0{}^*\delta)$. Cancel $C_v$. This is precisely the cocycle law, so step 4 defines $f_*$.

source.place: Tag 09VH, sentence "A similar argument shows that ... satisfies the cocycle condition", expanded with the same ordinary comparisons.

proof.text:
Let $(M,\beta)$ belong to $\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal R')$, and let $h:f_0^*M\to N$ have ordinary transpose $\widehat h:M\to F$. Equivariance of $\widehat h$ is equivalent, after multiplying by the invertible $b_s$, to
$$b_s\,(s')^*\widehat h\,\beta=f_{1,*}\gamma\,b_t\,(t')^*\widehat h.$$
Transpose this equality under $f_1^*\dashv f_{1,*}$. Step 3 identifies the transpose of $b_s(s')^*\widehat h$ with $s^*h$, and that of $b_t(t')^*\widehat h$ with $t^*h$. Naturality of the Hom bijection, equivalently [lem-sfb-adjunction-transpose-square], identifies the displayed equality with
$$s^*h\circ f_1^*\beta=\gamma\circ t^*h.$$
This is exactly equivariance of $h$. Since transposition is a bijection, this equivalence proves both directions required in the statement, not just one implication. Restrict the ordinary Hom bijection to these equal subsets. Naturality in $M,N$ is inherited from the ordinary adjunction: precomposition and postcomposition preserve equivariance by the functor constructions. Thus these restricted bijections specify $f^*\dashv f_*$.
